extraction_notes.note: The proof-sketch rule asks for rigor semi_formal on sketches, but the rigor rule (and the finishing step) forbids rigor on proofs; rigor was omitted and the sketches' proves edges carry alternative: true, the appendix proofs being the primary ones.

Appendix D restates each result through thm-restate macros (\ThmTaste* etc.) inside statementbox, which carry no text; no node was made for the restatements, and the full proofs get named proves edges from the section titles.
Author 'Fact' environments quoting cited results verbatim; typed theorem with origin external per Hard rule 4.
Cited results stated in running text without proof; typed theorem/external rather than claim since they restate prior results.
The two generators are defined by a case-split display; the algorithm node is the defining sentence and its two algorithm_steps are the two branch rows inside the numbered equation.

The count-budget paragraph argues and concludes in one go (remark, not claim); the closed-form wrapped-length sentence restates the later Digit-sum Lemma and was kept as a claim nested with its numbered equation.

Informal restatements of the results in the abstract and Contributions, the notation table (App. A), the results map (App. B), oracle/taxonomy tables, numerical tables, related work, practitioner FAQ and history appendices (E, F, H-K) were not extracted as nodes.

nodes.name: Ground set with canonical order
nodes.statement:
Fix a countable \emph{ground set} $U$ of statements with a fixed canonical total order
$\prec$, written $x_1 \prec x_2 \prec \cdots$.
nodes.section: 2.1 Ground set, generation in the limit, and breadth

nodes.name: Prefix L[1..M]
nodes.statement:
For an infinite $L \subseteq U$ we write
$\rest{L}{M}$ for the set of its first $M$ elements under $\prec$ (so $\rest{L}{M}$ is always
an initial segment of $L$ in $\prec$-order, and indexing is $1$-based: $\rest{L}{1} =
\{\min_\prec L\}$).
nodes.statement_short: L[1..M] denotes the first M elements of L in canonical order (1-based).
nodes.section: 2.1 Ground set, generation in the limit, and breadth

nodes.name: Language
nodes.statement:
A \emph{language} is an infinite subset of $U$; all languages in this
paper are infinite unless stated otherwise.
nodes.section: 2.1 Ground set, generation in the limit, and breadth

nodes.name: Kleinberg--Mullainathan (KM) enumeration
nodes.statement:
An adversary
fixes an unknown target language $H$ and a \emph{Kleinberg--Mullainathan (KM) enumeration}
of it: an infinite stream $w_1, w_2, \dots$ whose set of values is exactly $H$ (every
element of $H$ appears, repetitions allowed).
differentia: whose set of values is exactly $H$
nodes.section: 2.1 Ground set, generation in the limit, and breadth

nodes.name: Seen-set S_t
nodes.statement:
At round $t$ the generator has seen the
prefix and we write $S_t \coloneqq \{w_1, \dots, w_t\}$ for the \emph{seen-set}.
nodes.section: 2.1 Ground set, generation in the limit, and breadth

nodes.name: Set-valued generator
nodes.section: 2.1 Ground set, generation in the limit, and breadth

nodes.name: Exact and approximate breadth in the limit
nodes.statement:
We say $G$ achieves
\emph{exact breadth in the limit} on $H$ if there is $n^*$ with $G_n = H \setminus
 S_n$ for all $n \ge n^*$ (it outputs all and only the unseen valuable statements), and
\emph{approximate breadth in the limit} if eventually $G_n \subseteq H$ and $\abs{H
\setminus G_n} < \infty$.
nodes.statement_short: Exact breadth: eventually G_n = H minus S_n; approximate: eventually G_n inside H and missing finitely many.
nodes.section: 2.1 Ground set, generation in the limit, and breadth

nodes.name: Element-based generator
nodes.statement:
An \emph{element-based generator} maps the seen-set to a single new statement $a_t =
G(S_t) \in U$ with $a_t \notin S_t$; this is the convention of
\citet{kleinberg2026partial} (hereafter KW), used for the \emph{density} results of
\cref{sec:res-dichotomy}.
nodes.section: 2.1 Ground set, generation in the limit, and breadth

nodes.name: Limit set O
nodes.statement:
The object of study over an infinite run is the \emph{limit set} of
all outputs,
\begin{equation} O \coloneqq \{\, a_t : t \ge 1 \,\},
\end{equation}
the set of \emph{all} statements the generator ever emits across the entire run (KW
Definition~1.1).
nodes.section: 2.1 Ground set, generation in the limit, and breadth

nodes.name: Limit set
nodes.statement: O \coloneqq \{\, a_t : t \ge 1 \,\},
nodes.section: 2.1 Ground set, generation in the limit, and breadth
nodes.label: eq:limitset

nodes.name: Lower and upper prefix densities
nodes.statement:
To measure how much of a language a set covers we use prefix densities in the
canonical order: for $L' \subseteq L$,
\begin{equation} \dlow{L'}{L} \coloneqq \liminf_{N \to \infty} \frac{\abs{L' \cap \rest{L}{N}}}{N},
  \qquad
  \dup{L'}{L} \coloneqq \limsup_{N \to \infty} \frac{\abs{L' \cap \rest{L}{N}}}{N},
\end{equation}
writing $\dens{L'}{L}$ for the common value when the limit exists.
nodes.statement_short: Lower/upper density of L' in L: liminf/limsup of the fraction of L's first N elements lying in L'.
nodes.section: 2.1 Ground set, generation in the limit, and breadth

nodes.name: Prefix densities
nodes.statement:
\dlow{L'}{L} \coloneqq \liminf_{N \to \infty} \frac{\abs{L' \cap \rest{L}{N}}}{N},
  \qquad
  \dup{L'}{L} \coloneqq \limsup_{N \to \infty} \frac{\abs{L' \cap \rest{L}{N}}}{N},
nodes.section: 2.1 Ground set, generation in the limit, and breadth
nodes.label: eq:density

nodes.name: Angluin's condition
nodes.statement:
A countable collection $\mc{H}$ of languages satisfies
\emph{Angluin's condition} if every $L \in \mc{H}$ has a finite \emph{tell-tale} $T_L \subseteq
L$ such that no $L' \in \mc{H}$ with $T_L \subseteq L'$ is a proper subset of $L$.
nodes.statement_short: Every L in the collection has a finite tell-tale T_L not contained in any proper sub-language from the collection.
nodes.section: 2.1 Ground set, generation in the limit, and breadth

nodes.name: Weak Angluin condition
nodes.statement:
It satisfies
the \emph{weak Angluin condition} if the tell-tale separates $L$ from every $L' \in \mc{H}$
with $\abs{L \setminus L'} = \infty$ rather than from every proper subset.
nodes.section: 2.1 Ground set, generation in the limit, and breadth

nodes.name: Gold's non-identifiability of ascending chains
nodes.statement:
These are exactly
the conditions under which a Gold-style ascending chain $L_1 \subsetneq L_2 \subsetneq \cdots$
with union $\bigcup_j L_j$ in the collection \emph{fails} to be identifiable, since every
finite subset of the union lies in some proper sub-language of the chain
\citep{gold1967language}.
assumptions: a Gold-style ascending chain $L_1 \subsetneq L_2 \subsetneq \cdots$ with union $\bigcup_j L_j$ in the collection
nodes.statement_short: A Gold-style ascending chain with its union in the collection is not identifiable, since every finite subset of the union lies in a chain member.
nodes.section: 2.1 Ground set, generation in the limit, and breadth

nodes.name: Revealed core
nodes.statement:
Instead the adversary enumerates an infinite \emph{revealed
core} $C \subseteq H$ (the ``literature'': the valuable statements actually written
down) and may leave the rest of $H$ forever unseen.
nodes.section: 2.2 Partial enumeration and the revealed core

nodes.name: Core density alpha and legal instance
nodes.statement:
We parametrize the core by its lower
density in the target,
\begin{equation} \alpha \coloneqq \dlow{C}{H} ,
\end{equation}
and speak of an instance $(H, C, \text{enumeration})$ as \emph{legal} if the
enumeration is a repetition-free listing whose value-set is $C$.
nodes.section: 2.2 Partial enumeration and the revealed core

nodes.name: Core density
nodes.statement: \alpha \coloneqq \dlow{C}{H} ,
nodes.section: 2.2 Partial enumeration and the revealed core
nodes.label: eq:alpha

nodes.name: Generation in the limit with partial enumeration
nodes.statement:
In their statement, \emph{generation in the limit with
partial enumeration} means that ``for some time $t^*$, its outputs $a_t$ satisfy $a_t \in K -
S_t$ for all $t \ge t^*$'' \citep[\S1]{kleinberg2026partial}, where $K$ is the true language
and $S_t$ the enumerated prefix.
nodes.definiendum: generation in the limit with partial enumeration
nodes.section: 2.2 Partial enumeration and the revealed core

nodes.name: Partial-enumeration generation (KW Theorem 1.6)
nodes.statement:
There is an algorithm $\mathcal A$ that achieves generation in the limit with partial
enumeration with the following guarantee: ``for any adversarial enumeration $E$ of an infinite
subset $C$ of one of the languages $K \in \mathcal X$ such that $C$ has lower density at least
$\alpha > 0$ in $K$, the set of output strings $O(E, \mathcal A)$ $[\dots]$ has a lower
density in $K$ that is at least $\alpha/2$.'' Moreover, ``$\alpha/2$ also serves as an upper
bound on the lower density achievable by any algorithm.'' In our notation: for every countable
collection $\mathcal X$ there is an element-based generator with $\dlow{O}{H} \ge
\tfrac12\,\dlow{C}{H}$ on every legal instance, and from some round $t^*$ on it outputs
only elements of $H$.
assumptions:
for every countable
collection $\mathcal X$
conclusions:
there is an element-based generator with $\dlow{O}{H} \ge
\tfrac12\,\dlow{C}{H}$ on every legal instance, and from some round $t^*$ on it outputs
only elements of $H$.
nodes.statement_short: KW: some generator achieves lower density at least alpha/2 of the core density, and alpha/2 is optimal.
nodes.section: 2.2 Partial enumeration and the revealed core
nodes.label: fact:kw16

nodes.name: Chain validity in the partial model (KW Lemma 2.5(1))
nodes.statement:
For the identified-intersection sequence $\mathcal I^{(t)}$ that KW's generator maintains,
``there is a finite time $T$ such that after which all the identified intersection $\mathcal
I^{(t)}$ are valid,'' where valid means $\mathcal I^{(t)} \subset K$. The statement and its
proof are in the partial-enumeration model. In our notation: there is a finite round $T_0$
with $\mathcal I^{(t)} \subseteq H$ for all $t \ge T_0$.
conclusions:
there is a finite round $T_0$
with $\mathcal I^{(t)} \subseteq H$ for all $t \ge T_0$.
nodes.statement_short: KW's identified intersections are eventually contained in the true language.
nodes.section: 2.2 Partial enumeration and the revealed core
nodes.label: fact:kw25

nodes.name: Pair model
nodes.statement:
A \emph{pair model} is a countable collection $\mc{P} = \{(F_i, H_i)\}_i$ of pairs of
infinite languages with $H_i \subseteq F_i \subseteq U$. We call $F_i$ the
\emph{formal} language (its membership oracle is a proof checker) and $H_i$ the
\emph{valuable} language (the unknown target). The \emph{fiber} over a set $F$ is
\begin{equation} \fiber{F} \coloneqq \setbuild{H_i}{F_i = F},
\end{equation}
the collection of candidate targets sharing the formal world $F$ \emph{as a set}. The
adversary picks an index $z$, fixes $(F,H) = (F_z, H_z)$, and presents an
enumeration of its core (full enumeration of $H$ in the breadth setting).
nodes.statement_short: A countable collection of nested (formal, valuable) language pairs; the fiber over F is the set of targets sharing ambient F.
nodes.section: 2.3 The nested model: validity versus value
nodes.label: def:pairmodel

nodes.name: Fiber
nodes.statement: \fiber{F} \coloneqq \setbuild{H_i}{F_i = F},
nodes.section: 2.3 The nested model: validity versus value
nodes.label: eq:fiber

nodes.name: Verifier oracle
nodes.statement:
A \emph{relativized} (verifier-assisted) generator may, in each round, issue finitely many
adaptive membership queries to the indicator $\mathbf 1_{F}$ of the true formal language (a
perfect proof checker for the realized ambient) before producing its output. The query budget
per round is finite but unbounded; no computability is assumed (KMV Remark~2.3 conventions).
The adversary is \emph{non-effective}: it may decide infinitary conditions on the generator's
behavior. This is the standard convention for impossibility results in this line
\citep{kalavasis2024characterizations}.
nodes.statement_short: A relativized generator may make finitely many adaptive membership queries to the indicator of F each round; the adversary is non-effective.
nodes.section: 2.3 The nested model: validity versus value
nodes.label: def:verifier

nodes.name: Error trichotomy
nodes.statement:
At a round in which the generator emits $a$, with true pair $(F, H)$ and seen-set
$S_t$, the output is a \emph{hallucination} if $a \notin F$ (formally false), a
\emph{triviality} if $a \in F \setminus H$ (valid but worthless), and \emph{valuable} if
$a \in H \setminus S_t$ (a genuinely new valuable statement; being in $H \subseteq
 F$, it is in particular valid). Throughout, \emph{valid} refers to membership in the formal
world $F$, \emph{valuable} to membership in the target $H$. The \emph{triviality rate}
through round $N$ is
\begin{equation} \mathrm{trv}_N \coloneqq \frac{\abs{\{\, t \le N : a_t \in F \setminus H \,\}}}{N},
\end{equation}
and the \emph{trivia count} is $\abs{O \cap (F \setminus H)}$. We distinguish count
from rate throughout: a generator may emit infinitely many trivia at rate tending to $0$.
nodes.statement_short: Each output is a hallucination (not in F), a triviality (in F minus H) or valuable (new element of H); defines triviality rate and trivia count.
nodes.section: 2.3 The nested model: validity versus value
nodes.label: def:trichotomy

nodes.name: Triviality rate
nodes.statement: \mathrm{trv}_N \coloneqq \frac{\abs{\{\, t \le N : a_t \in F \setminus H \,\}}}{N},
nodes.section: 2.3 The nested model: validity versus value
nodes.label: eq:trv

nodes.name: Coverage, soundness, sound coverage
nodes.statement:
In the density setting, the \emph{coverage} of a generator at truth $H$ is $c \coloneqq
\dlow{O \cap H}{H}$, the lower density of the valuable statements it emits. A
generator is \emph{sound} if it never hallucinates: $a_t \in F$ for all $t$, i.e.\ $O
\subseteq F$. A set-valued generator achieves \emph{sound coverage in the limit} on $(F,
H)$ if there is $n^*$ with
\begin{equation} H \setminus S_n \;\subseteq\; G_n(S_n) \;\subseteq\; F
  \qquad \text{for all } n \ge n^*:
\end{equation}
it covers every unseen valuable statement while asserting only formally valid ones.
nodes.statement_short: Coverage is the lower density of valuable outputs; sound means never hallucinating; sound coverage sandwiches outputs between unseen value and F.
nodes.section: 2.3 The nested model: validity versus value
nodes.label: def:soundcov

nodes.name: Sound coverage sandwich
nodes.statement:
H \setminus S_n \;\subseteq\; G_n(S_n) \;\subseteq\; F
  \qquad \text{for all } n \ge n^*:
nodes.section: 2.3 The nested model: validity versus value
nodes.label: eq:soundcov

nodes.name: Breadth characterizations (KMV Theorems 3.3 and 3.8)
nodes.statement:
A countable collection $\mc{H}$ admits a set-valued
generator achieving exact breadth in the limit if and only if $\mc{H}$ satisfies Angluin's
condition (Theorem~3.3), and admits approximate breadth in the limit if and only if $\mc{H}$
satisfies the weak Angluin condition (Theorem~3.8).
assumptions: A countable collection $\mc{H}$
conclusions:
admits a set-valued
generator achieving exact breadth in the limit if and only if $\mc{H}$ satisfies Angluin's
condition (Theorem~3.3)

admits approximate breadth in the limit if and only if $\mc{H}$
satisfies the weak Angluin condition (Theorem~3.8)

admits a set-valued
generator achieving exact breadth in the limit if and only if $\mc{H}$ satisfies Angluin's
condition (Theorem~3.3)

admits approximate breadth in the limit if and only if $\mc{H}$
satisfies the weak Angluin condition (Theorem~3.8)

nodes.statement_short: Exact breadth iff Angluin's condition; approximate breadth iff the weak Angluin condition.
nodes.section: 2.3 The nested model: validity versus value
nodes.label: fact:kmv

nodes.name: Set-versus-element bridge
nodes.statement:
The two output conventions are reconciled by the standard set-versus-element bridge (a KW
analogue of KMV Lemma~2.3): a set-valued breadth statement and an element-based density
statement about the same family agree on which statements are eventually emitted.
nodes.origin_citation: standard; KW analogue of KMV Lemma 2.3
conclusions:
a set-valued breadth statement and an element-based density
statement about the same family agree on which statements are eventually emitted

nodes.name: Verification is not taste
nodes.statement:
Let $\mc{P} = \{(F_i, H_i)\}$ be a countable pair model (\cref{def:pairmodel}), with a
relativized generator (\cref{def:verifier}) that queries the perfect verifier $\mathbf
1_{F}$.
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\alph*)}]
  \item Exact breadth in the limit on $\mc{P}$ is achievable if and only if every fiber

Why part (c) of Verification is not taste holds
nodes.statement:
Part~(c) holds because the verifier's answers are determined by $F$ alone: in a
single-ambient model $F$ is known a priori, and within a fiber the oracle discriminates
nothing (part~(d)). Note also that (c) is scoped to breadth: for other goals, such as sound
coverage in \cref{sec:res-flood}, the verifier does strictly more. The contrast that makes (c)
sharp: a single \emph{negative} example inside $F \setminus H$ would collapse the
Angluin boundary entirely, but the verifier returns only ``valid'' on all of $F$ and so
never supplies one. Verification certifies the world; it does not reveal the worth of a
statement within it.

nodes.name: Proof sketch of the exhaustive generator and the separation
nodes.statement:
Part~(a) is immediate from $H \subseteq F$. For (b), the model $\mc{P}^{\dagger}$ is
built on a Gold-style chain $H_1 \subsetneq H_2 \subsetneq \cdots$ with union $L^*$ in
the collection. A sandwich-exclusion lemma (\cref{lem:sandwich}; \cref{fig:sandwich}) shows no

to fail on one of the realized instances; the construction is a \emph{non-effective}
adversary, the standard convention for impossibility results in this line
(\cref{def:verifier}). Part~(c) combines (a) and (b). Full proof in \cref{app:flood}.

Where the oracle identifies the ambient (and hence the target), as on $\mc{P}^{\dagger}$,

nodes.name: Exact density of the tight family
nodes.statement:
The point of \eqref{eq:Halpha} is that it realizes \emph{exact}
density for \emph{every} real $\alpha$, not merely rational $\alpha$:
\begin{equation} \abs{K \cap \rest{K'}{N}} = \lfloor \alpha N \rfloor
  \quad\text{for all } N, \qquad\text{hence}\qquad \dens{K}{K'} = \alpha \text{ exactly},
\end{equation}
and moreover $K \cap \rest{K'}{N} = \rest{K}{m_N}$ with $m_N = \lfloor \alpha N \rfloor$,
while $F \setminus K' = \{\text{odds}\}$ is infinite.
conclusions: \abs{K \cap \rest{K'}{N}} = \lfloor \alpha N \rfloor

nodes.name: The racing adversary
nodes.statement:
For infinite $K \subseteq U$, the \emph{racing adversary} $A_K$ enumerates, at every round
$t \ne 2^n$, the $\prec$-least element of $K \setminus (S_{t-1} \cup O_{t-1})$ (the
least string unused by either side), and at every round $t = 2^n$ the $\prec$-least element of
$(O_{t-1} \cap K) \setminus S_{t-1}$, recycling a generator-claimed element so that the
enumeration stays complete (falling back to the fresh rule if no such element exists).
nodes.statement_short: Enumerates the least unused element of K except at powers of two, where it re-enumerates a generator-claimed element.

nodes.name: Race lemma
nodes.statement:
Let $K \subseteq U$ be infinite and let $T_{\mathrm{race}} \subseteq \mathbb{N}$ have density
$1$, with $$w(t) \coloneqq t - \abs{T_{\mathrm{race}} \cap [1\dots t]} = o(t).$$
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(R\arabic*)}]
  \item \textup{(Greedy cover)} If at every $t \in T_{\mathrm{race}}$ the generator outputs
    the $\prec$-least element of $K \setminus (S_t \cup O_{t-1})$, then against every
    adversary enumeration, $\abs{O \cap \rest{K}{M}} \ge \tfrac12\,(M - w(\tau_M) - 1)$ for
    all $M$, where $\tau_M$ is the index of the $M$-th race round; hence $\dlow{O \cap
    K}{K} \ge 1/2$.
  \item \textup{(Racing cap)} The racing adversary $A_K$ of \cref{def:racingadv} is a legal
    repetition-free enumeration of $K$. Against it, every generator satisfies $\abs{O \cap
    \rest{K}{M}} \le M/2 + \log_2 M + 3$ for $M \ge 2$; hence $\dup{O \cap K}{K} \le 1/2$.
\end{enumerate}

Impossibility side of the dichotomy
nodes.statement:
On the tight family $\mc{H}_{\alpha}$ of \eqref{eq:Halpha}, with deterministic element-based generators
and limit-set coverage:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\alph*)}]
  \item \textup{(Race cap)} For every deterministic generator there are two legal instances of
    $\mc{H}_{\alpha}$ sharing one transcript (the adversary is $A_K$ inside $K$), with coverage at most
    $1/2$ at truth $K$ and at most $1 - \alpha/2$ at truth $K'$ (revealed core $C = K$,
    density $\alpha$). Hence no generator guarantees coverage exceeding $1 - \alpha/2$ on
    $\mc{H}_{\alpha}$, nor exceeding $1/2$ at truth $K$.
  \item \textup{(Finite-trivia cap)} Every deterministic generator that emits finitely many
    trivia on every legal instance has coverage at most $\alpha/2$ on the truth-$K'$ racing
    instance.

    $\alpha/2$ on all of $\mc{H}_{\alpha}$ emits infinitely many trivia on some instance; with
    \cref{thm:harvest}\textup{(iii)}, $\alpha/2$ is exactly the finite-trivia frontier.
\end{enumerate}

nodes.statement:
With the partial model and limit-set coverage:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}]
  \item \textup{(Universal sweep)} The generator $G_{\mathrm{sw}}$ of \eqref{eq:gharv} is
    sound (zero hallucination, unconditionally) and on every legal instance achieves $O
    \supseteq H \setminus C$, hence coverage $c \ge 1 - \dup{C}{H}$ ($\ge 1 -
    \alpha$ when $\dens{C}{H} = \alpha$ exists), with trivia rounds among $[1\dots N]$
    bounded by $T_0 + \lfloor \sqrt N \rfloor$ ($T_0$ finite, instance-dependent): the trivia
    rate tends to $0$ while the count is infinite in general (necessarily, by
    \cref{thm:caps}(c)).
  \item \textup{(Tight generator on $\mc{H}_{\alpha}$)} On the tight family $\mc{H}_{\alpha}$ the single
    deterministic generator $G^*$ of \eqref{eq:gstar} achieves, with zero hallucination:
    \begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\alph*)}]
  \item truth $K$ (any $C \subseteq K$, any order): $c \ge \max(1/2,\ 1 -
    \dup{C}{K})$, trivia rate $\le \lfloor \sqrt N \rfloor / N$;
  \item truth $K'$ with $C \subseteq K$ (covering all of \cref{thm:caps}(a)'s tight
    instances): $c \ge 1 - \alpha/2 - o(1)$, with zero trivia;
  \item truth $K'$ with $C \not\subseteq K$: $c \ge \max(1/2,\ 1 - \dup{C}{K'})$,
    zero trivia.

    eventually zero trivia; on $\mc{H}_{\alpha}$ it attains $\alpha/2$ at truth $K'$ and $1/2$ at truth
    $K$, matching \cref{thm:caps}'s caps.
\end{enumerate}

nodes.name: Proof sketch of the achievability side
nodes.statement:
A pointer lemma drives (i): any $x \in H \setminus C$ stays in $U_t$ (as $H$ is
consistent) and is never enumerated, so if it were never output the sweep rounds (of which
there are infinitely many) would always emit a new element strictly below $x$, which is
impossible, as only finitely many positions lie below $x$. For (ii), $G^*$ races on the
conjunction $I_t$ (which equals $K$ while the seen-set sits inside $K$) and sweeps on the
union $U_t = K'$, so race covers half of $K$ and the sweep claims all of $D = K' \setminus K$;
at truth $K'$ the two disjoint contributions sum to $1 - \alpha/2$. A key consistency point:

\subseteq F$, it is eventually sound and eventually zero-trivia, which is exactly what our
soundness and finite-trivia hypotheses require. Full proof in \cref{app:harvest}.

nodes.name: Consistency mechanism
nodes.statement:
At truth $K$, $G^*$ emits infinitely many elements of $D = F \setminus K$ (the sweep covers
the union $K' \supseteq D$), so its trivia count there is infinite. This is the mechanism that
reconciles \cref{thm:caps}(b) with \cref{thm:harvest}(ii): the finite-trivia cap of $\alpha/2$
governs only generators whose trivia count is finite on \emph{every} instance, and $G^*$ is
not one of them. The infinitude of $O \cap D$ at truth $K$ is precisely the resource that
pays for coverage $1 - \alpha/2$ at truth $K'$.

nodes.statement:
A digit-sum formula computes the wrapped length, $\abs{w}_{G \cup D_t} = \sum_i s_{b_t}(N_i)$

nodes.statement:
The
construction uses the macros $\mu_{m,i} \coloneqq x^i a\, x^{q+1-i} a\, x^{2^m}$ ($m \ge 1$, $1
\le i \le q$) and, under the bounded cut $\theta \equiv 1$ ($\Comp{D,1} = G \cup D$, the

  \ \subsetneq\

nodes.name: Free-monoid pairs realize the dichotomy
nodes.statement:
In $F_n$ ($n \ge 2$), with letters $\{a, x\}$:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}]
  \item \textup{(Name-cut pairs at every rational $\alpha$)} The pair \eqref{eq:namecut}
    satisfies $\abs{K \cap \rest{K'}{N}} = \alpha N + O(q)$, so $\dens{K}{K'} = \alpha$
    exactly; it meets the interface of \cref{rmk:interface}, and the dichotomy
    (\cref{cor:dichotomy}) holds verbatim inside the compression model.
  \item \textup{(Obstruction: the bounded cut is forced)} For the unbounded cut
    $\theta_\kappa$ with dictionary-only wrapped length and nested tag-dictionaries
    ($\hat\mu_{m,i} = a a\, x^i a\, x^{q+1-i} a\, x^{2^m}$, tags $\le p$ versus all), the
    analogous pair $(\hat K, \hat K')$ has $\dup{\hat K}{\hat K'} = 0$ (unique parsing via
    $aa$-blocks; the total count of compressible strings is exponential in $L$, the $k$-block
    counting $N_k(L) \le q^k (\log_2 L + 1)^k$ bounds the small-$k$ mass, and the tag
    restriction truncates the rest; the good-word fraction vanishes at rate $\Theta(1/\log L)$
    along prefix scales). Nested tag-pairs under unbounded cuts realize no $\alpha \in (0,1)$.
  \item \textup{(Extreme separation point)} For that pair $(\hat K, \hat K')$, finite-trivia
    sound generators have coverage $0$ at truth $\hat K'$ (same-transcript transfer and
    $\dup{\hat K}{\hat K'} = 0$), while $G_{\mathrm{sw}}$ of \cref{thm:harvest}(i) achieves
    coverage $1$ with vanishing trivia rate. The free regime exhibits the maximal gap of the
    dichotomy: coverage $0$ versus $1$.
\end{enumerate}

nodes.name: Imprecision of exhaustive generation
nodes.statement:
In $A_n$ with base $c \ge 4$ and $\kappa < n(1 - 1/\log_2 c)$, the compressible sublanguage $H
= \Comp{D_c}$ satisfies
\begin{equation} c_1\, r^{\,1/\log_2 c - n} \ \le\ \frac{\abs{H \cap B_G(r)}}{\abs{B_G(r)}}
  \ \le\ c_2\, r^{-\delta}, \qquad \delta = n - \kappa - n/\log_2 c > 0,
\end{equation}
where $B_G(r)$ is the wrapped-length ball of radius $r$. The fraction of compressible
statements is polynomially small in the radius $r$, equivalently exponentially small in ABFM's
compressed scale $s$ (since $r = c^{\Theta(s)}$; interpretation only). The exhaustive
generator's precision thus tends to $0$ polynomially in volume, while the sweep generator's
precision tends to $1$.
assumptions: In $A_n$ with base $c \ge 4$ and $\kappa < n(1 - 1/\log_2 c)$
conclusions:
The exhaustive
generator's precision thus tends to $0$ polynomially in volume, while the sweep generator's
precision tends to $1$.
nodes.statement_short: The fraction of compressible elements in a wrapped-length ball is polynomially small in the radius.

nodes.name: Numerical sanity checks
nodes.statement:
The density claims were sanity-checked numerically using the limit-set methodology: fix the
prefix size $N$, grow the run length $T$, and compute coverages in exact rational arithmetic
to avoid floating-point artifacts in the density limits. The race share converges to $1/2$,
and on $\mc{H}_{\alpha}$ with $\alpha = 1/3$ the truth-$K'$ coverage of $G^*$ converges to $5/6 = 1 -
\alpha/2$ while a pure-race generator stalls at $\alpha/2 \approx 0.17$. See
\cref{app:numerics} for the details.
nodes.statement_short: Exact-arithmetic simulations confirm race share 1/2 and G* coverage 5/6 at alpha = 1/3, while pure race stalls at alpha/2.

nodes.name: The count budget collapses
nodes.statement:
One might hope for a finer hierarchy between the finite and the infinite trivia regimes,
indexed by a count budget $g(N)$ on the trivia emitted in the first $N$ rounds. There is none.
Our achievability proof shows that the sweep claims every never-enumerated valuable string
under \emph{any} unbounded trivia allowance, so every $g(N)\to\infty$ already buys the full
$1-\alpha/2$ (\cref{thm:harvest}); the finite-trivia cap $\alpha/2$ is exactly the
complementary case (\cref{thm:caps}). The dichotomy is genuinely \emph{count-finite versus
count-infinite}, full stop, and not the coarse shadow of a smoother trade-off.
nodes.statement_short: No finer hierarchy between finite and infinite trivia: any unbounded trivia budget already achieves 1 - alpha/2.

nodes.name: The singleton sparse-core race
nodes.statement:
\emph{The singleton sparse-core race.} On the tight family the recorded core is the
    conjunction of the candidates and is raceable at exactly $1/2$. When the core is an
    unstructured sparse set (a singleton collection), a bottom-racing adversary outruns any
    core-blind generator, and the optimal share of the recorded mass is governed by
    combinatorics we have not resolved. We conjecture the optimum is $1-\alpha$ for $\alpha\le
    1/2$; settling it is a cat-and-mouse problem about which the present techniques are
    silent.
nodes.statement_short: Optimal recorded-mass share when the core is an unstructured sparse set, against a bottom-racing adversary.

We conjecture the optimum is $1-\alpha$ for $\alpha\le

$\alpha\le

nodes.name: Partial enumeration of structured chains
nodes.statement:
\emph{Partial enumeration of structured chains.} \cref{thm:abelian} establishes
    breadth for abelian refinement chains in the breadth model; the behavior of their relative
    densities under partial enumeration, whether the structured regime that needs no trivia
    for breadth also escapes them for density, is open.

nodes.name: Statistical rates
nodes.statement:
\emph{Statistical rates.} We work distribution-free and in the limit. A relativization
    of the rate analysis of \citet{kalavasis2025limits} to the nested pair, quantifying how
    fast coverage approaches its optimum, is left open.

nodes.name: Computational and efficient versions
nodes.statement:
\emph{Computational and efficient versions.} Our generators are arbitrary functions of
    the prefix; whether the dichotomy survives a computability or efficiency constraint, in
    the spirit of the complexity barriers of \citet{arenas2025complexity}, is open in the
    nested model.

nodes.name: Oracle-free sound coverage characterization
nodes.statement:
\emph{Oracle-free sound coverage.} \cref{thm:flood}(b) exhibits one pair model on
    which no oracle-free generator achieves sound coverage, but we do not characterize which
    pair models admit it. We ask for an Angluin-type condition on $\mc{P}$ (a combinatorial
    property of the candidate pairs) deciding whether oracle-free sound coverage
    (equivalently, the sandwich property of \eqref{eq:soundcov}) is achievable; our separation
    gives one failure, a full characterization is open.
nodes.statement_short: Find an Angluin-type condition on pair models deciding when oracle-free sound coverage is achievable.

nodes.name: Monoid
nodes.statement: A \emph{monoid} is a set with an associative binary operation and an identity element.
nodes.genus: set with an associative binary operation

nodes.name: Free abelian monoid A_n
nodes.statement:
\emph{The free abelian monoid $A_n$} on generators $a_1, \dots, a_n$ is the set of formal
products $\prod_{i=1}^n a_i^{N_i}$ with $N_i \in \mathbb{N}$, multiplied coordinate-wise; it is
isomorphic to $(\mathbb{N}^n, +)$, with each element identified with its exponent vector $(N_1, \dots,
N_n)$.

nodes.name: Raw length
nodes.statement: The \emph{raw length} (the generator count) is $\abs{w}_G = \sum_{i=1}^n N_i$.

nodes.name: Degree-then-lex order on A_n
nodes.statement:
We order
$A_n$ by degree-then-lex: first by $\abs{w}_G$, then lexicographically on the exponent vector.

nodes.name: Free monoid F_n
nodes.statement:
\emph{The free monoid $F_n$} on $n$ letters is the set of finite words over the alphabet, with
concatenation as the operation and the empty word as identity; $\abs{w}_G$ is the word length.

nodes.name: Length-then-lex order on F_n
nodes.statement: We order $F_n$ by length-then-lex.

nodes.name: Canonical orders are isomorphic to N
nodes.statement:
Both orders are order-isomorphic to $\mathbb{N}$ (\cref{fig:monoids}; each has finitely many elements
below any given one, and the order is total), which is exactly the structure the density
machinery of \cref{sec:prelim-km} requires: a countable ground set with a canonical order in
which $\rest{L}{N}$ is a well-defined initial segment.

nodes.name: Dictionary and macros
nodes.statement:
Following ABFM, a \emph{dictionary} $D$ is a finite or infinite set of designated monoid
elements, called \emph{macros}.

nodes.name: Augmented generating set and factorization
nodes.statement:
Generation is allowed to use the \emph{augmented generating
set} $G \cup D$: a factorization of $w$ is an expression of $w$ as a product of elements of $G
\cup D$.

nodes.name: Wrapped length
Wrapped length
nodes.statement: \abs{w}_{G \cup D} \coloneqq \min \set*{\, k : w = g_1 \cdots g_k,\ g_j \in G \cup D \,}
nodes.label: eq:wraplen

nodes.name: Geometric dictionary
nodes.statement:
For $A_n$ the relevant dictionaries are \emph{geometric}: $D_c = \{\, c^{\,j} a_i : i \le n,\
j \ge 1 \,\}$ provides single-letter powers at every scale $c^j$.

nodes.name: Closed form of wrapped length (digit sum)
nodes.statement:
For this dictionary the
wrapped length has a closed form,
\begin{equation} \abs{w}_{G \cup D_c} = \sum_{i=1}^n s_c(N_i),
\end{equation}
where $s_c(N)$ is the sum of the base-$c$ digits of $N$ (\cref{fig:macro}) (the digit-sum
lemma, \cref{lem:digitsum}; the minimizing factorization is the base-$c$ representation of
each coordinate).
conclusions: \abs{w}_{G \cup D_c} = \sum_{i=1}^n s_c(N_i),
nodes.statement_short: Under a geometric dictionary the wrapped length is the sum of base-c digit sums of the exponents.

nodes.name: Digit-sum closed form
nodes.statement: \abs{w}_{G \cup D_c} = \sum_{i=1}^n s_c(N_i),
nodes.label: eq:bg-digitsum

nodes.name: Compressibility cut and compressible sublanguage
nodes.statement:
The \emph{compressibility cut} is the threshold
\begin{equation} \theta_\kappa(L) \coloneqq \kappa \log_2(1 + L),
\end{equation}
and the \emph{compressible sublanguage} is
\begin{equation} \Comp{D} \coloneqq \set*{\, w : \abs{w}_{G \cup D} \le \theta_\kappa(\abs{w}_G) \,},
\end{equation}
the elements whose wrapped length is logarithmic in their raw length.
also_stated_at:
We work in the abelian monoid $A_n$ and the free monoid $F_n$, each with its canonical order
isomorphic to $\mathbb{N}$ (as \cref{lem:race,thm:caps} demand), and write $\Comp{D} \coloneqq \{\, w :
\abs{w}_{G \cup D} \le \theta_\kappa(\abs{w}_G)\,\}$ for the sublanguage compressible under a
macro dictionary $D$, where $\abs{w}_{G \cup D}$ is the wrapped length and $\theta_\kappa(L) =
\kappa \log_2(1+L)$ the compressibility cut (\cref{app:background} collects the definitions
and the macro framework).
nodes.statement_short: theta_kappa(L) = kappa log2(1+L); H_D collects elements whose wrapped length is at most the cut of their raw length.

nodes.name: Bounded cut
Proof of Verification is not taste
nodes.statement:
We prove (a) and (b) together (necessity, then sufficiency), then (c) and (d) and the edge
cases.

\medskip\noindent\textbf{Necessity.}\quad
Suppose some fiber $\fiber{F^*}$ violates the relevant condition. Write $\mc{H} \coloneqq
\fiber{F^*}$; it is countable, nonempty, and all its members are infinite. Restrict the
adversary to instances $(F^*, H)$ with $H \in \mc{H}$. On every such instance the
verifier handed to a relativized generator $G$ is always the single fixed function $\mathbf
1_{F^*}$. Define the oracle-stripped ordinary generator
\begin{equation} G'_n(S_n) \coloneqq G_n^{\,\mathbf 1_{F^*}}(S_n).
\end{equation}
This is well defined: in round $n$ the generator's adaptive query tree has finite depth, and
the fixed function $\mathbf 1_{F^*}$ resolves every query, selecting one leaf and one
output. Thus $G'_n$ is an arbitrary set-valued function of the prefix, exactly the object KMV
quantify over (\cref{fact:kmv}; their Remark~2.3 imposes no computability). Extensional
agreement holds across all of $\mc{H}$: for every fiber instance and every enumeration,
\begin{equation} G_n^{\,\mathbf 1_{F_z}}(S_n) = G'_n(S_n)
  \quad\text{for all } n \tag{$*$}
\end{equation}
because $F_z = F^*$ for every $z$ indexing a member of the fiber, so the oracle is the
identical function. Now if $G$ achieved exact (resp.\ approximate) breadth in the limit on all
of $\mc{P}$, then by \eqref{eq:extagree} the ordinary generator $G'$ would achieve it on every
target in $\mc{H}$, contradicting \cref{fact:kmv}, since $\mc{H}$ violates Angluin's (resp.\ the
weak Angluin) condition. Hence the condition is necessary in each part.

\medskip\noindent\textbf{Sufficiency.}\quad
Assume every fiber satisfies the relevant condition.

\emph{Stage~1 (ambient identification; sample-independent).} In round $n$ the generator
queries the canonical point $x_n$ to the verifier. Call index $i$ \emph{ambient-consistent at
$n$} if $F_i \cap \{x_1, \dots, x_n\} = F \cap \{x_1, \dots, x_n\}$, and let $\hat z_n$
be the least ambient-consistent index (the set is nonempty since the true index $z$
qualifies).

\begin{lemma}[Stage-1 stabilization] $\hat z_n$ stabilizes in finite time to $z_0 \coloneqq \min\{ i : F_i = F \}$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
$z_0$ is ambient-consistent at every $n$, so $\hat z_n \le z_0$ always. Each $i < z_0$ has
$F_i \ne F$ (by minimality of $z_0$), hence there is a least canonical point $x_{m(i)}
\in F_i \mathbin\triangle F$, and $i$ is permanently inconsistent from round $m(i)$ on.
Taking $N_1 \coloneqq \max_{i < z_0} m(i) < \infty$, every $i < z_0$ is eliminated by round
$N_1$, so $\hat z_n = z_0$ for all $n \ge N_1$. (No distinctness of the $F_i$ is needed;
duplicates share the fiber.)
\end{proof}

\emph{Stage~2 (fiber generation).} For each ambient set $F$ that occurs, fix, by the
achievability half of \cref{fact:kmv} applied to the fiber $\fiber{F}$, an ordinary
generator $\Gamma^{(F)}$ achieving exact (resp.\ approximate) breadth in the limit on
$\fiber{F}$. (The choice ranges over the countably many occurring ambient sets; we use the
axiom of choice over this countable index, removable by taking the $\prec$-lexicographically
least generator in a fixed enumeration; see the closing remark.) The constructions' internal
mechanics are absorbed into the fixed function level; no computability is claimed.

Define the composite relativized generator
\begin{equation} G_n^{\,\mathbf 1_{F}}(S_n) \coloneqq \Gamma^{(F_{\hat z_n})}_n(S_n).
\end{equation}
For $n \ge N_1$, \cref{lem:s1} gives $F_{\hat z_n} = F$, so
\begin{equation} G_n^{\,\mathbf 1_{F}}(S_n) = \Gamma^{(F)}_n(S_n)
  \quad\text{for } n \ge N_1. \tag{$\dagger$}
\end{equation}
The true target $H = H_z$ lies in the true fiber $\fiber{F}$ (witnessed by $z$), and
$S_n$ is the genuine prefix of a genuine KM enumeration of $H$: the generator never
restarts the enumeration at $N_1$. By the guarantee of $\Gamma^{(F)}$ there is a finite
round $n^*_\Gamma$ from which the breadth property holds; for $n \ge \max(N_1, n^*_\Gamma)$,
\eqref{eq:dagger} transfers it to $G$. The pre-stabilization rounds form a finite prefix,
absorbed by ``in the limit''. This proves (a) and (b).

\medskip\noindent\textbf{(c).}\quad
In the single-ambient case the verifier is the fixed function $\mathbf 1_{F}$ from
round~$1$, so \eqref{eq:extagree} gives relativized $\iff$ oracle-free, and both $\iff$ (weak)
Angluin by \cref{fact:kmv}. Thus, for the breadth goal, the verifier's only information
content in the pair model is the identification of $F$ performed in Stage~1; within a fiber
it changes nothing. (The scope is essential: \cref{thm:flood} shows that for the
sound-coverage goal the verifier does strictly more.)

\medskip\noindent\textbf{(d).}\quad
For $H_i, H_j$ in the same fiber, $\mathbf 1_{F_i} = \mathbf 1_{F_j} = \mathbf
1_{F}$ literally. The adaptive query tree, resolved by $\mathbf 1_{F}$ on a fixed prefix
$S_n$, yields the identical path and identical output regardless of which of $H_i,
H_j$ is the true target. Hence any behavioral distinction within a fiber is driven by the
enumeration alone.

\medskip\noindent\textbf{Edge cases.}\quad
\textsc{(E1) Duplicates.} Angluin's conditions are properties of the underlying set system and
are invariant under repetition of languages in the collection. \textsc{(E2) Finite fibers.} A
finite fiber satisfies Angluin's condition: for each ordered pair $i \ne j$ with $H_i
\setminus H_j \ne \emptyset$, place a witness $t_{ij} \in H_i \setminus H_j$ into the
tell-tale $T_i$ (at most $m-1$ elements for a fiber of size $m$); then any $H_j \supseteq
T_i$ forces $H_i \subseteq H_j$, so $H_j$ is not a proper subset of $H_i$.
\textsc{(E3)} Only occurring ambients are ever guessed, and occurring fibers are nonempty
(they contain the realized target). \textsc{(E4)} The same valuable language appearing under
two different ambients constitutes two different instances in two different fibers; Stage~1
separates them by the ambient query.

\medskip\noindent\textbf{Choice avoidance.}\quad
The use of the axiom of choice in Stage~2 is cosmetic. Fix once and for all a canonical
enumeration of all ordinary generators (e.g.\ a $\prec$-lexicographic order on finite
descriptions); for each occurring ambient $F$, let $\Gamma^{(F)}$ be the
lexicographically least generator achieving the required breadth on $\fiber{F}$. This is a
definable choice, so no appeal to the axiom of choice is needed.

nodes.statement:
Call $x$ \emph{resolved at $t$} if $x \in S_t \cup O_t$.

\medskip\noindent\textbf{(R1).}\quad
Let $t_M$ be the first round at which all of $\rest{K}{M}$ is resolved.
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{Step \arabic*.}, leftmargin=3.4em]
  \item At any race round $t \in T_{\mathrm{race}}$ with $\rest{K}{M}$ not yet resolved before
    the output, the output is a \emph{new} element of $O \cap \rest{K}{M}$. Indeed the rule
    outputs the $\prec$-least element of $K \setminus (S_t \cup O_{t-1})$, and the
    $\prec$-least unresolved element of $K$ lies in the downward-closed set $\rest{K}{M}$
    (some element of $\rest{K}{M}$ is unresolved, and the global minimum over $K$ of
    unresolved elements is $\preceq$ it, hence in $\rest{K}{M}$).
  \item Consequently $t_M \le \tau_M$: each of the (at most) $M$ race rounds up to $t_M$ that
    finds $\rest{K}{M}$ unresolved contributes a distinct element of $\rest{K}{M}$, and $M$
    such contributions exhaust $\rest{K}{M}$.
  \item At most one race round $\le t_M$ is non-contributing: by minimality of $t_M$,
    $\rest{K}{M}$ is unresolved at every race round strictly before $t_M$, so each such round
    contributes; only the round $t_M$ itself may be non-contributing (it may resolve the last
    element via the seen-set). Hence $\abs{O \cap \rest{K}{M}} \ge t_M - w(t_M) - 1$, where
    $w(t_M)$ counts the non-race rounds up to $t_M$.
  \item \emph{Steal bound.} Each $x \in \rest{K}{M} \setminus O$ is resolved only by
    entering $S_{t_M}$; distinct elements have distinct first-enumeration rounds $\le
    t_M$, so $\abs{\rest{K}{M} \setminus O} \le t_M$.
\end{enumerate}
Adding Step 3 and Step 4, $2\abs{O \cap \rest{K}{M}} \ge M - w(t_M) - 1 \ge M - w(\tau_M) -
1$ (using $t_M \le \tau_M$ and monotonicity of $w$). Since $\tau_M = M + w(\tau_M) \sim M$ and
$w = o(t)$, dividing by $M$ and taking the liminf gives $\dlow{O \cap K}{K} \ge 1/2$.

\medskip\noindent\textbf{(R2).}\quad
\emph{Legality of $A_K$.} At $t \ne 2^n$ the adversary enumerates the $\prec$-least element of
$K \setminus (S_{t-1} \cup O_{t-1})$ (a fresh round); at $t = 2^n$ it enumerates the
$\prec$-least element of $(O_{t-1} \cap K) \setminus S_{t-1}$ (a recycle round,
draining the generator's hoarded backlog from the bottom; if empty, it uses the fresh rule as
a fallback). We claim every $x \in K$ is enumerated at some finite round, so $A_K$ is a legal
repetition-free enumeration of $K$. The $\prec$-least un-enumerated element of $K$ advances
monotonically: fresh rounds push it forward, and recycle rounds drain the $O$-backlog from
the bottom, so no element below the current pointer can be hoarded forever. Hence every fixed
$x \in K$ is enumerated at a finite round. No rate is claimed or needed: legality is eventual
only.

\emph{The cap.} Fix $M \ge 2$. Let $F_M$ be the set of fresh-enumerated elements in
$\rest{K}{M}$ and $G_M = O \cap \rest{K}{M}$.
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(C\arabic*)}, leftmargin=3.4em]
  \item $F_M \cap G_M = \emptyset$ (an element is either enumerated by the adversary or output
    by the generator first, in the sense that an output element $a_t \notin S_t$ is not
    among the fresh-enumerated by definition of the rule), so $\abs{F_M} + \abs{G_M} \le M$.
  \item \emph{Injection $G_M \to F_M$ up to exceptions.} Map the entry round $t$ of an
    $O$-element to round $t+1$. If $t+1$ is a fresh round and $\rest{K}{M}$ is not yet
    fresh-exhausted, the fresh rule at $t+1$ enumerates an element of $F_M$. There are exactly
    two kinds of exception, which we count separately:
    \begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}, leftmargin=2.4em]
  \item \emph{power-of-two recycle rounds:} rounds $t$ with $t+1 = 2^n$. Up to the
    fresh-exhaustion round $E_M$ (defined next) there are at most $\lfloor \log_2 E_M \rfloor
    + 1$ of these;
  \item \emph{the single post-exhaustion threshold:} after $E_M$ the fresh rule no longer
    enumerates a new element of $\rest{K}{M}$, costing $O(1)$ further exceptions.
    \end{enumerate}
Hence the total number of exceptions is at most $\lfloor \log_2 E_M \rfloor + 1 + O(1) \le
\log_2 E_M + 2$.
  \item \emph{The fresh-exhaustion round $E_M$.} Define $E_M$ as the round by which every
    element of $\rest{K}{M}$ is used (lies in $S \cup O$), equivalently the round by
    which the fresh pointer has passed $K[M]$, skipping any $O$-hoarded elements. We bound
    $E_M$ non-circularly. Each fresh round outputs the $\prec$-least un-enumerated element of
    $K$, so fresh claims strictly $\prec$-increase the fresh pointer; within $M$ fresh rounds
    the pointer therefore passes $K[M]$. Writing $T \coloneqq E_M$, the number of non-fresh
    (recycle) rounds up to $T$ is at most $\lfloor \log_2 T \rfloor + 1$ (one per power of two
    $\le T$), so the number of fresh rounds up to $T$ is at least $T - \log_2 T - 1$.
    Requiring this to reach $M$ gives the implicit bound $T \le M + \log_2 T + 1$; solving it
    yields $E_M \le M + \log_2(M+1) + 2$.
\end{enumerate}
Combining (C1)--(C3): $\abs{O \cap \rest{K}{M}} = \abs{G_M} \le \abs{F_M} + (\log_2 E_M +
2) \le M/2 + \log_2 M + 3$, using $E_M \le M + \log_2(M+1) + 2$ so that $\log_2 E_M \le \log_2
M + O(1)$. Dividing by $M$ and taking the limsup gives $\dup{O \cap K}{K} \le 1/2$.

\emph{Caution on $E_M$.} The round $E_M$ must \emph{not} be read as the round of full
enumeration of $\rest{K}{M}$: against a hoarding generator, full enumeration of $\rest{K}{M}$
can take exponentially many rounds (the recycle trickle drains the backlog one element per
power-of-two round). The cap argument needs only fresh-exhaustion, which advances at rate $1$
per fresh round.

$\prec$-least element of $(O_{t-1} \cap K) \setminus S_{t-1}$ (a recycle round,
draining the generator's hoarded backlog from the bottom; if empty, it uses the fresh rule as
a fallback). We claim every $x \in K$ is enumerated at some finite round, so $A_K$ is a legal
repetition-free enumeration of $K$. The $\prec$-least un-enumerated element of $K$ advances
monotonically: fresh rounds push it forward, and recycle rounds drain the $O$-backlog from
the bottom, so no element below the current pointer can be hoarded forever. Hence every fixed
$x \in K$ is enumerated at a finite round. No rate is claimed or needed: legality is eventual
only.

\emph{The cap.} Fix $M \ge 2$. Let $F_M$ be the set of fresh-enumerated elements in
$\rest{K}{M}$ and $G_M = O \cap \rest{K}{M}$.
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(C\arabic*)}, leftmargin=3.4em]

    $O$-element to round $t+1$. If $t+1$ is a fresh round and $\rest{K}{M}$ is not yet
    fresh-exhausted, the fresh rule at $t+1$ enumerates an element of $F_M$. There are exactly
    two kinds of exception, which we count separately:

    fresh-exhaustion round $E_M$ (defined next) there are at most $\lfloor \log_2 E_M \rfloor
    + 1$ of these;

    enumerates a new element of $\rest{K}{M}$, costing $O(1)$ further exceptions.

nodes.statement:
\medskip\noindent\textbf{(a).}\quad
Run any deterministic generator $G$ against the racing adversary $A_K$ of \cref{lem:race}(R2).
The transcript is a single object $O$, and any verifier is fixed advice ($F = \mathbb{N}$ under
both readings), so the two readings $K$ and $K'$ share it.

\emph{Legality of both readings.} As truth $K$, $A_K$ is a full repetition-free enumeration of
$K$ (\cref{lem:race}(R2)). As truth $K'$, the same stream is a legal partial enumeration of
$K'$ with revealed core $C = K$ of exact density $\dens{K}{K'} = \alpha$
(\eqref{eq:exactdensity}).

\emph{Truth $K$.} By \cref{lem:race}(R2), $c \le \dup{O \cap K}{K} \le 1/2$, i.e.\
coverage $\le 1/2 + O(\log M)/M$.

\emph{Truth $K'$.} Split $\rest{K'}{N} = \rest{K}{m_N} \sqcup (D \cap \rest{K'}{N})$ with $m_N
= \lfloor \alpha N \rfloor$ (by \eqref{eq:exactdensity}). Then
\begin{align*}
  \abs{O \cap \rest{K'}{N}}
  &\le \abs{O \cap \rest{K}{m_N}} + \abs{D \cap \rest{K'}{N}}\\
  &\le \bigl(\tfrac{m_N}{2} + \log_2 m_N + 3\bigr) + (N - m_N)
  = N - \tfrac{m_N}{2} + O(\log N),
\end{align*}
using \cref{lem:race}(R2) on the $K$-part. Dividing by $N$ and taking the liminf gives $c
\le 1 - \alpha/2$, i.e.\ coverage $\le 1 - \alpha/2 + O(\log N)/N$.

\emph{Per-instance.} The caps bind for every generator on the single instance $A_K$; no
adaptivity to the realized truth is used. Hence no generator guarantees coverage exceeding $1
- \alpha/2$ on $\mc{H}_{\alpha}$, nor exceeding $1/2$ at truth $K$.

\medskip\noindent\textbf{(b).}\quad
Run $G$ against the same $A_K$, so the transcript is shared. Suppose $G$ emits finitely many
trivia on every legal instance; in particular at the legal truth-$K$ instance, $\abs{O \cap
(F \setminus K)} < \infty$, so $C_0 \coloneqq \abs{O \cap D} < \infty$. At truth $K'$,
\begin{equation*}
  \abs{O \cap \rest{K'}{N}}
  \le \abs{O \cap K \cap \rest{K'}{N}} + C_0 .
\end{equation*}
Applying \cref{lem:composition} with $A = O \cap K$ and then \cref{lem:race}(R2),
\begin{equation*}
  c = \dlow{O \cap K'}{K'}
  \le \dup{O \cap K}{K'}
  = \alpha \cdot \dup{O \cap K}{K}
  \le \alpha \cdot \tfrac12 = \tfrac{\alpha}{2}.
\end{equation*}

\medskip\noindent\textbf{(c).}\quad
The contrapositive of (b): any generator guaranteeing coverage exceeding $\alpha/2$ on all of
$\mc{H}_{\alpha}$ must emit infinitely many trivia on some instance. Exactness of the finite-trivia
frontier at $\alpha/2$ follows from \cref{thm:harvest}(iii), which attains $\alpha/2$ at truth
$K'$ with eventually zero trivia.
nodes.statement_short: Run any generator against the racing adversary: one transcript is legal at truths K and K'; cap the K-part by (R2), and for finite trivia carry the cap through density composition.

\medskip\noindent\textbf{Pointer lemma.}\quad
We first prove the fact that drives both generators.

\begin{lemma}[Pointer lemma] Suppose at each sweep round $t \in R$ the generator outputs the $\prec$-least element of $V_t
\setminus (S_t \cup O_{t-1})$ for a family $V_t$ with $H \subseteq V_t$ for all $t$,
and $R$ is infinite. Then for every $x \in H$ never enumerated by the adversary, $x \in
 O$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
Fix such an $x$ at $H$-position $p$. Since $H \subseteq V_t$ always, $x \in V_t$; since
$x$ is never enumerated, $x \notin S_t$ for all $t$. Suppose $x \notin O$. At every
sweep round $t \in R$, the output is the $\prec$-least element of $V_t \setminus (S_t \cup
 O_{t-1})$, which is $\preceq x$ (as $x$ itself is available) and $\ne x$ (as $x \notin
 O$), hence strictly $\prec x$ --- a new element of $H$ strictly below position $p$. But
only $p-1$ positions lie below $x$, and $R$ is infinite, a contradiction. Hence $x \in O$.
\end{proof}

\paragraph{(i) Universal sweep $G_{\mathrm{sw}}$.}
Recall $U_t = \bigcup\{H' \in \mc{H} : S_t \subseteq H'\}$ and the sweep schedule $R =
\{k^2\}$. Apply \cref{lem:pointer} with $V_t = U_t$: for any $x \in H \setminus
 C$, $H$ is consistent ($S_t \subseteq C \subseteq H$) so $H \in
\mc{H}_t$ and $x \in U_t$, while $x \notin C$ is never enumerated. Hence $O \supseteq
 H \setminus C$. Therefore
\begin{equation*}
  \abs{O \cap \rest{H}{N}} \ge N - \abs{C \cap \rest{H}{N}},
  \qquad\text{so}\qquad
  c \ge 1 - \dup{C}{H},
\end{equation*}
which is $\ge 1 - \alpha$ when $\dens{C}{H} = \alpha$ exists. \emph{Trivia rate.} By
\cref{fact:kw25} there is a finite $T_0$ with $\mathcal I^{(t)} \subseteq H$ for all $t \ge
T_0$, so every non-sweep output from $T_0$ on lies in $H$; the only possible trivia rounds
among $[1\dots N]$ are the $\le T_0$ early non-sweep rounds and the $\lfloor \sqrt N \rfloor$
sweep rounds, giving a trivia count $\le T_0 + \lfloor \sqrt N \rfloor$ and rate $\to 0$. The
count is infinite in general, necessarily so, by \cref{thm:caps}(c). \emph{Soundness.} $U_t
\subseteq \bigcup \mc{H} \subseteq F$; $\mathcal I^{(t)}$ is contained in some candidate
$\subseteq F$; the fallback lies in $F$. Hence $O \subseteq F$: zero
hallucination.

(The restated KW lemma is used only for the non-sweep half of the trivia bound. A bare
conjunction default would fail on a general $\mc{H}$: for $\mc{H} = \{\mathbb{N} \setminus \{n\}\}$ the
conjunction of consistent candidates is just $S_t$. On $\mc{H}_{\alpha}$, $G^*$ below avoids this
restated lemma entirely.)

\medskip\noindent\textbf{(ii) Tight generator $G^*$ on $\mc{H}_{\alpha}$.}\quad
Recall $\mc{H}_t = \{H' \in \mc{H}_{\alpha} : S_t \subseteq H'\}$, $I_t = \bigcap \mc{H}_t$, $U_t =
\bigcup \mc{H}_t$. The structure is:
\begin{equation*}
  S_t \subseteq K \ \Longrightarrow\ \mc{H}_t = \{K, K'\},\ I_t = K,\ U_t = K';
  \qquad
  S_t \not\subseteq K \ \Longrightarrow\ \mc{H}_t = \{K'\},\ I_t = U_t = K'.
\end{equation*}

\emph{(a) Truth $K$.} Here every enumerated element is in $C \subseteq K$, so $S_t
\subseteq K$ always and $I_t = K$. The non-sweep rounds form the set $\mathbb{N} \setminus R$, of
density $1$ with $w(t) = \lfloor \sqrt t \rfloor = o(t)$; on them $G^*$ runs
\cref{lem:race}(R1)'s greedy race on $K$ (the $\prec$-least element of $I_t \setminus (S_t
\cup O_{t-1}) = K \setminus (S_t \cup O_{t-1})$). Thus $\dlow{O \cap K}{K} \ge
1/2$, i.e.\ $c \ge 1/2$. Applying \cref{lem:pointer} with $V_t = U_t = K' \supseteq K$
gives $O \supseteq K \setminus C$, so $c \ge 1 - \dup{C}{K}$; together $c \ge
\max(1/2, 1 - \dup{C}{K})$. \emph{Trivia.} Race outputs lie in $K$; the sweep covers $U_t
= K' \supseteq D$, so trivia rounds among $[1\dots N]$ number $\le \lfloor \sqrt N \rfloor$,
rate $\to 0$. Note $O \cap D = D$ is \emph{infinite}: the sweep eventually claims all of
$D$ via \cref{lem:pointer} (each $d \in D$ lies in $U_t = K'$ and is never enumerated at truth
$K$). This infinitude is exactly why \cref{thm:caps}(b)'s finite-trivia cap does not apply to
$G^*$.

\emph{(b) Truth $K'$ with $C \subseteq K$.} The transcript is identical to case (a):
$C \subseteq K$ means $S_t \subseteq K$ throughout, so $G^*$ cannot and need not
distinguish the two truths, and runs (R1)'s race on $K$ exactly as before. By
\cref{lem:pointer} with $H = K'$ (every $x \in K' \setminus C$ is never enumerated and
lies in $U_t = K'$), $O \supseteq K' \setminus C \supseteq D$. For coverage, split
$\rest{K'}{N} = \rest{K}{m_N} \sqcup (D \cap \rest{K'}{N})$ ($m_N = \lfloor \alpha N
\rfloor$); the sweep claims all $N - m_N$ elements of $D \cap \rest{K'}{N}$ and the race
claims at least $m_N/2 - O(\sqrt N)$ of $\rest{K}{m_N}$, and the two parts are disjoint, so
\begin{equation*}
  \abs{O \cap \rest{K'}{N}} \ge (N - m_N) + \tfrac{m_N}{2} - O(\sqrt N)
  = N\bigl(1 - \tfrac{\alpha}{2}\bigr) - O(\sqrt N),
\end{equation*}
giving $c \ge 1 - \alpha/2 - o(1)$. \emph{Trivia.} Race outputs $\subseteq K \subseteq K'$
and sweep outputs $\subseteq K'$, so \emph{zero} trivia at truth $K'$.

\emph{(c) Truth $K'$ with $C \not\subseteq K$.} Let $t_0$ be the first (finite) round with
$w_{t_0} \notin K$. From $t_0$ on, $S_t \not\subseteq K$, so $I_t = U_t = K'$. Apply
\cref{lem:race}(R1) with $K \leftarrow K'$ and $T_{\mathrm{race}} = (\mathbb{N} \setminus R) \setminus
[1\dots t_0]$ (still density $1$): $c \ge 1/2$. \Cref{lem:pointer} with $V_t = U_t = K'$
gives $c \ge 1 - \dup{C}{K'}$; together $c \ge \max(1/2, 1 - \dup{C}{K'})$. All
outputs lie in $K'$, so zero trivia.

\emph{Scope.} The unqualified ``$1 - \alpha/2$ at truth $K'$'' is false for general $C
\subseteq K'$: if $C = K'$ enumerated by the racing adversary, the cap of
\cref{lem:race}(R2) holds with $K \leftarrow K'$ and pins every generator at $1/2$. Case (b)'s
restriction $C \subseteq K$ is exactly the regime the dichotomy needs.

\medskip\noindent\textbf{(iii) Finite-trivia side (restated).}\quad
By \cref{fact:kw16}, KW's generator achieves $\dlow{O}{H} \ge \tfrac12
\dlow{C}{H}$ for every countable collection, never consulting $F$; generation in the
limit gives $\exists t^*\, \forall t \ge t^*: a_t \in H \setminus S_t$, so the trivia
rounds are confined to $t < t^*$: eventually zero. Because $H \subseteq F$, the same
statement $a_t \in H$ for $t \ge t^*$ makes the generator \emph{eventually sound} ($a_t \in
 F$) as well; this is exactly what our model's soundness (eventually $a_t \in F$) and
finite-trivia (eventually $a_t \notin F \setminus H$) hypotheses require, and it follows
from the generation guarantee alone. No claim about the pre-$t^*$ outputs (and in particular
no inference from the internal pod construction of KW's generator) is needed for the
load-bearing path. On $\mc{H}_{\alpha}$ this yields $\alpha/2$ at truth $K'$ and $1/2$ at truth $K$,
matching the caps of \cref{thm:caps}.

\begin{remark}[Non-load-bearing aside] KW's pods are in fact candidate-contained at all times, so one expects the pre-$t^*$ outputs
also to lie in $F$ here; we record this only as an aside, as the eventual-soundness
argument above already supplies everything the dichotomy uses.
\end{remark}

\textbf{(iii) Finite-trivia side (restated).}\quad
By \cref{fact:kw16}, KW's generator achieves $\dlow{O}{H} \ge \tfrac12
\dlow{C}{H}$ for every countable collection, never consulting $F$; generation in the
limit gives $\exists t^*\, \forall t \ge t^*: a_t \in H \setminus S_t$, so the trivia
rounds are confined to $t < t^*$: eventually zero. Because $H \subseteq F$, the same
statement $a_t \in H$ for $t \ge t^*$ makes the generator \emph{eventually sound} ($a_t \in
 F$) as well; this is exactly what our model's soundness (eventually $a_t \in F$) and
finite-trivia (eventually $a_t \notin F \setminus H$) hypotheses require, and it follows
from the generation guarantee alone. No claim about the pre-$t^*$ outputs (and in particular
no inference from the internal pod construction of KW's generator) is needed for the
load-bearing path. On $\mc{H}_{\alpha}$ this yields $\alpha/2$ at truth $K'$ and $1/2$ at truth $K$,

nodes.statement:
Write $w = \prod_i a_i^{N_i} \in A_n \cong (\mathbb{N}^n, +)$, identified with its exponent vector
$(N_1, \dots, N_n)$. We use three lemmas.

\begin{lemma}[Digit-sum formula] For the geometric dictionary $D_c = \{ c^{\,j} a_i : i \le n, j \ge 1 \}$ (with $c = b_t$),
the wrapped length is $\abs{w}_{G \cup D_c} = \sum_{i=1}^n s_c(N_i)$, where $s_c(N)$ is the
sum of the base-$c$ digits of $N$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
Each coordinate $a_i^{N_i}$ is factored independently (the dictionary words are single-letter
powers). For one coordinate: a factoring corresponds to a representation of $N_i$ as a sum of
powers of $c$ with nonnegative integer coefficients (multiplicities), and its symbol count is
the sum of those multiplicities. Replacing $c$ copies of the macro $c^{\,j} a_i$ by one copy
of $c^{\,j+1} a_i$ preserves the represented power and strictly decreases the symbol count, so
every minimizing representation has all multiplicities $< c$; the unique representation with
all multiplicities $< c$ is the base-$c$ representation of $N_i$. Hence the minimum symbol
count is its digit sum $s_c(N_i)$. Summing over coordinates gives the formula.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[Nesting] $\Comp{D_{t+1}} \subseteq \Comp{D_t}$, so $\{\Comp{D_t}\}_t$ is a descending chain.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
Since $b_{t+1} = b_t^2$, we have $D_{t+1} \subseteq D_t$. A richer dictionary cannot increase
the minimal factoring length, so $\abs{w}_{G \cup D_t} \le \abs{w}_{G \cup D_{t+1}}$ for every
$w$. Therefore every $w$ with $\abs{w}_{G \cup D_{t+1}} \le \theta_\kappa(\abs{w}_G)$ also
satisfies $\abs{w}_{G \cup D_t} \le \theta_\kappa(\abs{w}_G)$: membership transfers downward
and the chain is descending.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[Witness / singleton tell-tale] $w_t \coloneqq a_1^{\,b_t + b_t^3} \in \Comp{D_t} \setminus \Comp{D_{t+1}}$, and $T_t = \{w_t\}$
is a tell-tale for $\Comp{D_t}$ in the chain.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
By \cref{lem:digitsum}, $\abs{w_t}_{G \cup D_t} = s_{b_t}(b_t + b_t^3) = 2$ (the number $b_t +
b_t^3$ has base-$b_t$ digits $1$ at positions $1$ and $3$). In base $b_{t+1} = b_t^2$, the
same number is $b_t + b_t \cdot b_t^2 = b_t(1 + b_t^2)$, whose base-$b_t^2$ digit sum is $2
b_t$ (a digit $b_t$ at positions $0$ and $1$). The raw length is $\abs{w_t}_G = b_t + b_t^3$,
so $\theta_\kappa(\abs{w_t}_G) = \kappa \log_2(1 + b_t + b_t^3) \le 5\kappa \log_2 b_t$ for
large $b_t$. Then $\abs{w_t}_{G \cup D_t} = 2 \le \theta_\kappa$, so $w_t \in \Comp{D_t}$;
while $\abs{w_t}_{G \cup D_{t+1}} = 2 b_t > 5\kappa \log_2 b_t \ge \theta_\kappa$ since $b \ge
16\kappa^2$ forces $2 b_t > 5\kappa \log_2 b_t$, so $w_t \notin \Comp{D_{t+1}}$. As the chain
is descending, $\{w_t\}$ separates $\Comp{D_t}$ from every proper sub-language
$\Comp{D_{t'}}$, $t' > t$: any $\Comp{D_{t'}} \ni w_t$ would need $t' \le t$, so no proper
sub-language contains the tell-tale. The languages are infinite (e.g.\ all $a_1^{c^j}$ have
wrapped length $1$).
\end{proof}

The three lemmas give a strictly descending chain of infinite languages with singleton
tell-tales, so $\mc{H}_{\mathrm{ab}}$ satisfies Angluin's condition. By \cref{thm:taste}(a),
applied in the single fiber $F = A_n$, exact breadth in the limit is achievable: in the
abelian regime valuable generation needs no trivia. (The partial-enumeration behavior of the
chain, its relative densities, is open.)
nodes.statement_short: Three lemmas (digit-sum formula, nesting, singleton witness) give a strictly descending chain with singleton tell-tales; then apply Verification is not taste (a).

nodes.statement:
\medskip\noindent\textbf{(i) Name-cut pairs.}\quad
With the bounded cut $\theta \equiv 1$, the compressible language is exactly the nameable
corpus $\Comp{D,1} = G \cup D$: the letters $\{a, x\}$ together with the macro words. Each
$\mu_{m,i} = x^i a\, x^{q+1-i} a\, x^{2^m}$ has a \emph{unique} parsing (the two $a$'s mark
the boundaries, and the three $x$-blocks have lengths $i$, $q+1-i$, $2^m$ recovering $m, i$
unambiguously), so the words are distinct and the $a$-position encodes $i$. Order $F_n$ by
length-then-lex. For each $m$, the $q$ words $\{\mu_{m,i}\}_{i=1}^q$ form an equal-length
stratum (all have length $q + 3 + 2^m$), lex-ordered by $i$ via the position of the first $a$.
Of these $q$ words, the $p$ with $i \le p$ lie in $K$; so within each stratum the count of
$K$-elements is $p$ out of $q$. Summing over strata up to position $N$,
\begin{equation*}
  \abs{K \cap \rest{K'}{N}} = \alpha N + O(q),
  \qquad \alpha = p/q,
\end{equation*}
the $O(q)$ accounting for the partial last stratum and the two letters. Hence $\dens{K}{K'} =
\alpha$ exactly. The pair $(K, K', F_n)$ meets the interface of \cref{rmk:interface}: $F_n$ is
countable with the length-then-lex canonical order; $K \subsetneq K' \subseteq F_n$ are
infinite; $F_n \setminus K'$ is infinite (it contains all non-macro words); and $m_N = \alpha
N + O(q) = \alpha N + O(1)$. By \cref{rmk:interface}, \cref{lem:race,thm:caps} hold verbatim
for this pair, so the dichotomy (\cref{cor:dichotomy}) holds inside the compression model.

\medskip\noindent\textbf{(ii) Obstruction.}\quad
Now use the unbounded cut $\theta_\kappa$ with dictionary-only wrapped length and the nested
tag-dictionaries built from $\hat\mu_{m,i} = a a\, x^i a\, x^{q+1-i} a\, x^{2^m}$ (the leading
$aa$-block is a unique delimiter). Parsing is unique via the $aa$-blocks. Write $\mathcal
N(L)$ for the number of compressible strings of length $\le L$, and $N_k(L)$ for those parsing
into exactly $k$ tag-blocks ($k \ge 0$). We bound the upper density $\dup{\hat K}{\hat K'}$ in
five displayed steps.

\emph{(1) Deletion injection.} Map a $k$-block word ($k \ge 1$) to the $(k-1)$-block word
obtained by deleting its first $aa$-block (and the empty word for $k = 1$). A preimage of a
given image is recovered by choosing the deleted block: a tag $i \in [q]$ and a scale $m \le
\log_2 L$, so each image has at most $1 + q(\log_2 L + 1)$ preimages. Hence
\begin{equation} \mathcal N(L) \ \le\ \bigl(1 + q + q\log_2 L\bigr)\,\mathcal N(L-1).
\end{equation}

\emph{(2) Small-$k$ mass.} A length-$\le L$ word with $k$ blocks chooses, per block, a tag $i
\le q$ and a scale $2^m \le L$ (i.e.\ $m \le \log_2 L$), so $N_k(L) \le q^k(\log_2 L+1)^k$.
For $B \coloneqq \lceil 2 \log\log L / \log(q/p) \rceil$,
\begin{equation} \sum_{k \le B} N_k(L) \ \le\ B\, q^B (\log_2 L + 1)^B
  \ =\ \exp\!\bigl(O((\log\log L)^2)\bigr).
\end{equation}

\emph{(3) Tag truncation.} A $k$-block word lies in $\hat K$ only if all $k$ tags satisfy $i
\le p$ (versus all $i \le q$ for $\hat K'$). For $k > B$ this costs a factor at most
\begin{equation} (p/q)^k \ \le\ (p/q)^B \ =\ (\log L)^{-2}
\end{equation}
on the corresponding mass, by the choice of $B$.

\emph{(4) Lower bound on $\mathcal N$.} The true count is exponential in $L$; we need only the
weaker
\begin{equation} \mathcal N(L) \ \ge\ \exp\!\bigl(c\,\log L \cdot \log\log L\bigr),
\end{equation}
witnessed at the block count $k^* = \lfloor \kappa \log_2(1 + \sqrt L) \rfloor$: force one
scale near $\sqrt L$ so every word passes the cut $\theta_\kappa$, and choose the remaining
$k^*-1$ scales freely below $\sqrt L/k^*$. This weaker bound suffices.

\emph{(5) Conclusion.} Split the $\hat K$-mass at $B$ blocks. By \eqref{eq:smallk} the $k \le
B$ part is $\exp(O((\log\log L)^2))$; by \eqref{eq:tagtrunc} the $k > B$ part is at most
$(\log L)^{-2}\,\mathcal N(L)$. With \eqref{eq:delinj} and $N \ge \mathcal N(L-1)$,
\begin{align} \frac{\abs{\hat K \cap \rest{\hat K'}{N}}}{N}
  \ &\le\ \frac{\exp(O((\log\log L)^2)) + (\log L)^{-2}\,\mathcal N(L)}{\mathcal N(L-1)} \notag\\
  \ &\le\ o(1) + (\log L)^{-2}\bigl(1 + q + q\log_2 L\bigr)
  \ =\ \Theta(1/\log L),
\end{align}
using \eqref{eq:Nlower} to absorb the $\exp(O((\log\log L)^2))$ term into $o(1)$. The bound
\eqref{eq:goodfrac} holds along the prefix scales $N = \mathcal N(L-1)$; interpolating between
consecutive scales (the count grows by the factor \eqref{eq:delinj} between $L-1$ and $L$)
gives the same $o(1)$ rate for general $N$. Hence \[ \dup{\hat K}{\hat K'} \ =\ 0 : \] nested
tag-pairs under the unbounded cut realize no $\alpha \in (0,1)$. This is why the bounded cut
$\theta \equiv 1$ is \emph{forced} for the name-cut construction shape; we present (i) as a
worked example and (ii) as its obstruction, not as a generic compressible-language theorem.

\medskip\noindent\textbf{(iii) Extreme separation point.}\quad
For the pair $(\hat K, \hat K')$ of (ii): run any finite-trivia sound generator against the
racing enumeration of $\hat K$ as the revealed core. As in \cref{thm:caps}(b), the same
transcript serves both truths, and $\dup{\hat K}{\hat K'} = 0$ forces the coverage at truth
$\hat K'$ to satisfy $c \le \dup{\hat K}{\hat K'} = 0$ plus the finite-trivia correction
$C_0/N \to 0$; hence coverage $0$ at truth $\hat K'$. On the other hand, $G_{\mathrm{sw}}$ of
\cref{thm:harvest}(i) achieves $c \ge 1 - \dup{C}{\hat K'} = 1$ (since
$\dup{C}{\hat K'} = \dup{\hat K}{\hat K'} = 0$) with vanishing trivia rate. The free
regime thus exhibits the maximal gap of the dichotomy: coverage $0$ versus $1$.

Proof of imprecision of exhaustive generation
nodes.statement:
Work in $A_n$ with base $c \ge 4$ and $\kappa < n(1 - 1/\log_2 c)$. The wrapped-length ball
$B_G(r) = \{ w : \abs{w}_G \le r \}$ has volume $\abs{B_G(r)} = \Theta(r^n)$ (the number of
exponent vectors $(N_1, \dots, N_n)$ with $\sum_i N_i \le r$). By \cref{lem:digitsum}, $w \in
H = \Comp{D_c}$ iff $\sum_i s_c(N_i) \le \theta_\kappa(\abs{w}_G) = \kappa \log_2(1 +
\abs{w}_G) \le \kappa \log_2(1 + r)$.

\emph{Upper bound.} The number of vectors with $\sum_i s_c(N_i) \le \kappa \log_2 r$ and
$\sum_i N_i \le r$ is at most the number of vectors whose total base-$c$ digit sum is at most
$D \coloneqq \kappa \log_2 r$, each coordinate $< c^{\,L}$ with $L = \log_c r$. A standard count
of nonnegative integer vectors with bounded digit sum gives $\abs{H \cap B_G(r)} \le c_2'\,
r^{\,n/\log_2 c + \kappa}$ up to logarithmic factors; dividing by $\abs{B_G(r)} = \Theta(r^n)$
gives
\begin{equation*}
  \frac{\abs{H \cap B_G(r)}}{\abs{B_G(r)}} \le c_2\, r^{-\delta},
  \qquad \delta = n - \kappa - n/\log_2 c > 0,
\end{equation*}
where $\delta > 0$ by the hypothesis $\kappa < n(1 - 1/\log_2 c)$.

\emph{Lower bound.} Restrict to vectors all of whose coordinates are powers of $c$ (digit sum
$1$ each, total $\le n \le \kappa \log_2 r$ for large $r$): there are $\Theta((\log_c r)^n) =
\Theta((\log r)^n)$ of these within $B_G(r)$, but a stronger family gives the stated rate.
Take a single coordinate to range over base-$c$ blocks of magnitude up to $r^{1/\log_2 c}$
(digit sum $1$, the rest fixed); these lie in $H \cap B_G(r)$ and number $\Theta(r^{1/\log_2
c})$. Dividing by $\Theta(r^n)$ gives $\abs{H \cap B_G(r)}/\abs{B_G(r)} \ge c_1\,
r^{\,1/\log_2 c - n}$.

The two sides of \eqref{eq:precision} do \emph{not} have matching exponents: the upper bound
decays as $r^{-\delta}$ with $\delta = n - \kappa - n/\log_2 c$, while the lower bound decays
as $r^{1/\log_2 c - n}$, and $\delta \ne n - 1/\log_2 c$ in general (they differ by $\kappa +
(n-1)/\log_2 c$). The bound therefore brackets the precision between two polynomial rates
without pinning it; closing the gap, determining the exact polynomial exponent, is open.

Combining the two sides gives \eqref{eq:precision}. The fraction is polynomially small in the
radius $r$. Interpreting $r$ as ABFM's compressed scale via $r = c^{\Theta(s)}$ turns the
polynomial-in-$r$ decay into an exponential-in-$s$ decay (interpretation only, not used in the
bound). The exhaustive generator thus has precision tending to $0$ polynomially in volume,
while the sweep generator of \cref{thm:harvest}(i) has precision tending to $1$.

Combining the two sides gives \eqref{eq:precision}. The fraction is polynomially small in the
radius $r$. Interpreting $r$ as ABFM's compressed scale via $r = c^{\Theta(s)}$ turns the
polynomial-in-$r$ decay into an exponential-in-$s$ decay (interpretation only, not used in the
bound). The exhaustive generator thus has precision tending to $0$ polynomially in volume,
while the sweep generator of \cref{thm:harvest}(i) has precision tending to $1$.

The dichotomy by hand: a worked miniature
nodes.statement:
Take the
tight family \eqref{eq:Halpha} at $\alpha = 1/2$: the coverable world is the evens $K' =
\{0, 2, 4, \dots\}$, the revealed target is every second even, $K = \{2, 6, 10, \dots\}$
(the residue $2 \bmod 4$), the difference is $D = \{0, 4, 8, \dots\}$ (the residue $0 \bmod
4$), and the ambient is $F = \mathbb{N}$, so the odds sit idle throughout: neither player ever
touches them. The adversary is the racing adversary $A_K$ of \cref{def:racingadv}, which
enumerates fresh $\prec$-least elements of $K$ except at rounds $t = 2^n$, where it
re-enumerates an element the generator has already claimed. The generator is the tight
generator $G^*$ of \eqref{eq:gstar}, which sweeps the union $U_t = K'$ at square rounds $t
\in R = \{1, 4, 9, 16, \dots\}$ and races the intersection $I_t = K$ otherwise. Within a
round the adversary moves first; the generator sees $S_t$ and $O_{t-1}$.
\Cref{tab:miniature} replays the first twenty rounds; the trace, the prefix counts, and the
coverage figures below are machine-generated and machine-checked.
